A1.justification: Both PDFs describe MovieBench. Their main text, supplementary material, figures, tables, and equations are readable and support matching retained content against additions.

before.justification: v1 reports original annotation-quality assessments and experiments on keyframe generation, video generation, talking-human generation, and supplementary customized audio generation.

after.justification: v2 retains these original experiments and adds a human-voting study in supplementary Section 6.

M1.justification: The character-bank construction, sequential scene breakdown, multimodal shot annotation, and audio/subtitle pipelines remain unchanged. The added human study evaluates the existing metric without changing the method.

E1.justification: Table 1 adds an unexplained MovieBench 'Ours++' row reporting 116.8 hours alongside the retained 69.2-hour corpus. Section 3.1 still describes 91 movies and the same training/test split. The added corpus's composition and actual experimental use are unspecified, preventing a reliable judgment about changed coverage beyond dataset size.

E2.justification: The comparator memberships in the retained benchmark tables are unchanged. The new human study reuses AutoStory, Magic-Me, and CogVideoX. Newly cited NUWA-XL and Phenaki are explicitly excluded from evaluation.

E3.justification: v2 adds a human-voting evaluation comparing preferences with F1_ID across three existing models. This introduces an additional evaluation procedure, although participant counts, sample counts, and voting instructions are unspecified. The original benchmark settings and 85/6 movie split remain unchanged.

E4.justification: New supplementary Section 6 and Figure 10 examine agreement between automatic character-consistency scores and human preferences. The earlier character-consistency, viewpoint, temporal-description, and hallucination case studies are retained.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals, or significance tests for the benchmark results. The added user study reports voting percentages and qualitative correlation, without uncertainty estimates or a statistical correlation test.

E6.justification: Figure 10 adds human-voting shares of 43.40% for AutoStory, 25.20% for Magic-Me, and 31.40% for CogVideoX, alongside their unchanged F1_ID scores. Table 1 adds Ours++ corpus statistics. Numerical results in the original Tables 2–8 remain unchanged.

T1.justification: The character-bank definition, scene-breakdown equation, and metric definitions are retained. Although v2 omits the true-positive formula from the shortened main-text explanation, the same formula remains in supplementary Table 9. No new theoretical results or proofs appear.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same central contributions: a hierarchical movie-generation dataset, character appearance/audio consistency, and challenges involving multiple characters, viewpoints, and narrative progression. Condensed wording does not materially change these claims.

C2.justification: The new user-study discussion interprets matching model rankings as agreement between F1_ID and human judgment. It also suggests that human preferences capture qualitative factors missing from the metric. Existing generation limitations and the GPT-4-o hallucination discussion remain substantively unchanged.

D1.justification: The dataset access link, annotation and correction instructions, baseline implementation information, and audio preprocessing specifications are retained. No substantive new hyperparameters, hardware information, or reproducibility instructions accompany the additions.

R1.justification: Section 4.1 adds references to NUWA-XL and Phenaki and explains their exclusion through the authors' stated concerns about character consistency and open-source availability. The broader related-work discussion and research positioning remain unchanged.

P1.justification: v2 condenses introduction, metric, and experiment prose; adds a supplementary User Study section; and adds corresponding-author and funding acknowledgements. Existing supplementary sections are renumbered, while the overall narrative structure is retained.

P2.justification: v2 adds the Figure 10 voting bar chart and an Ours++ row in Table 1, shortens Table 5's caption, and reflows existing displays. Earlier appendix figures are retained and renumbered, and the conclusion now shares the final main-text page.

improvement.justification: The new human-voting comparison provides a limited empirical check of the character-consistency ranking that v1 lacked, while the explicit baseline-exclusion rationale improves transparency. These are modest gains: the study omits sampling details and uncertainty, and the Ours++ statistics lack an accompanying explanation of composition or experimental use. The original benchmark evidence remains intact.
